questions.question: How are night terrors (pavor nocturnus) distinguished from nightmares?

options.A: Night terrors occur during REM sleep and are clearly remembered; nightmares occur during NREM sleep and are forgotten
options.B: Night terrors occur during Stage 4 NREM sleep early in the night with complete amnesia; nightmares occur during REM sleep, usually later in the night, and are clearly remembered
options.C: There is no real difference between the two conditions
options.D: Both occur exclusively in adults, never in children

questions.explanation: Night terrors are a Stage 4 NREM parasomnia occurring in the first third of the night, with autonomic arousal (tachycardia, sweating) and complete amnesia for the event on waking. Nightmares, by contrast, occur during REM sleep (more common in the last third of the night) and are vividly and clearly remembered.
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.sourceChapter: Sleep Disorders — Parasomnias, Stage 4 Sleep Disorders
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: In studying road traffic accidents, why might 'accidents per 1000 vehicles' or 'per million vehicle-miles' be a more useful denominator than total population?

options.A: Total population is always the best denominator regardless of context
options.B: Because many people in the total population do not own or use vehicles, so vehicle-based denominators better reflect actual exposure/risk
options.C: Vehicle-based denominators are only used for aesthetic reasons with no analytical value
options.D: Total population data is impossible to obtain in any country

questions.explanation: When the denominator is more closely related to actual exposure to risk (like the number of vehicles or vehicle-miles travelled) rather than the whole population — many of whom may not drive or use vehicles at all — the resulting rate more accurately reflects the true risk of the event being measured.

questions.question: HELLP syndrome consists of:

questions.question: Cardiac muscle cannot be tetanised because of its:

questions.question: Commonest deformity in congenital dislocation of hip:

questions.question: LDL cholesterol is considered the ‘bad’ cholesterol because it:

questions.question: A patient status post CVA rocks back and forth in a supine position with legs flexed and arms clasped around his knees. Expected therapeutic outcomes include all of the following except:

options.A: Decreased extensor spasticity in the lower extremities
options.B: Inhibition of flexor spasticity in the upper extremities
options.D: Facilitation of extensor tone in the trunk

questions.explanation: Rocking with knees clasped does not facilitate trunk extensor tone; it inhibits spasticity and promotes protraction.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)

questions.question: Wound contraction is mediated mainly by:

questions.question: A 63-year-old female status post stroke is screened for admission into a rehabilitation hospital. A part of the screen the therapist utilizes a standardized instrument to document the extent of the patient's impairments and disabilities. Which of the following standardized instruments would be most beneficial to provide an assessment of motor function?
questions.explanation: The Fugl-Meyer Assessment documents motor impairment after stroke.

questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient diagnosed with an acute posterior cruciate sprain. The mechanism of injury for the posterior cruciate is:

options.A: A forceful landing on the anterior tibia with the knee hyperflexed
options.B: An anteriorly directed force applied to the tibia when the foot is fixed
options.C: A valgus force applied to the knee when the foot is fixed

questions.explanation: The PCL is injured by a force to the anterior tibia with the knee flexed, such as a dashboard impact.

questions.question: The most active form of thyroid hormone is:

questions.question: Avulsion fracture of the anterior inferior iliac spine is because of the violent contraction of the:

questions.question: Trigger finger is most likely to be associated with:

questions.question: A postoperative rigid dressing provides a patient status post amputation with all of the following advantages except:

options.A: Allows for daily inspection and dressing changes
options.B: Allows for earlier ambulation with a pylon attachment
options.D: Reduces the length of time necessary for shrinking of the limb

questions.explanation: A rigid dressing limits oedema and allows early pylon ambulation but, unlike a soft dressing, does not allow daily inspection of the wound.

questions.question: The original faradic current was:

questions.question: Visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) is transmitted by:

questions.question: The commonest deformity at hip in post polio residual paralysis is:

questions.question: A patient status postspinal fusion is referred for chest physical therapy. The therapist instructs patient in diaphragmatic breathing exercises.
